interpretation: Sorting by full identity inside hash-range partitions recovered a substantial portion of the compression lost by sorting random hash values and retained one scanned file per tested point. It still writes 49.4% slower and stores 38.8% more active Parquet than the sequential-identity baseline. Do not adopt this as the default layout from this fixture.

next_static_design_direction.reasoning: The two hash-range variants each add an exchange and sort before Delta write, improve one-file point scan evidence versus the hash-only baseline candidate counts but both lose on write cost and compressed size against the sequential identity layout. A staging representation change may remove CPU/temporary allocation without disturbing the already effective identity row order; its impact is unmeasured and requires separate code review, not another scale matrix.
next_static_design_direction.recommendation: Keep the baseline identity-preserving row order unless production input locality requires reshaping. Investigate the actual production staging path for avoidable key stringification and BIGINT reparsing while preserving exact keys and payload/custody strings. This is orthogonal to persisted layout and avoids adding another hash-range shuffle.
